bls-atus-2025.name: BLS American Time Use Survey, 2025 results

household-activities.name: Household activities (housework, food preparation, lawn care)
household-activities.passage: On an average day, 81 percent of people engaged in household activities

housework-gender-gap.name: Women spend more time on household activities than men
housework-gender-gap.passage: On the days they did household activities, women spent an average of 2.8

childcare-young-kids.name: Primary childcare in households with children under 6
childcare-young-kids.passage: Adults living in households with children under age 6 spent an average of 2.3 hours per day

childcare-gender-gap.name: Women spend more time on primary childcare than men
childcare-gender-gap.passage: women spent an hour more than men providing primary childcare to household children--2.8 hours compared to 1.7

work-hours.name: Hours worked on days worked (full-time employed)
work-hours.passage: On days they worked, full-time employed people worked an average of 8.1 hours.

watching-tv.name: Watching TV, the leisure activity taking the most time
watching-tv.passage: Watching TV was the leisure and sports activity that occupied the most time (2.6 hours per day)

not-enough-time.name: Do not have enough time to do what they want
not-enough-time.passage: the 48% who say they do not have enough time to do what they want to do is not much different from the 47% average

working-not-enough-time.name: Working Americans without enough time
working-not-enough-time.passage: About six in 10 working Americans (61%) say they do not have enough time to do what they want

parents-not-enough-time.name: Parents of children under 18 without enough time
parents-not-enough-time.passage: Sixty-one percent of those with children younger than 18 say they do not have enough time

pew-rushed-2005.name: Pew Research Center: Who's feeling rushed? (2005 survey)

always-rushed.name: Always feel rushed
always-rushed.passage: about a quarter (23%) of all adults in this country say they always feel rushed

working-mothers-rushed.name: Working mothers who always feel rushed
working-mothers-rushed.passage: Some 41% of them say they always feel rushed, compared with 25% of stay-at-home mothers of minor children

pew-smartphone-2026.name: Pew Research Center: time spent on smartphones (September 2026)

too-much-smartphone.name: Spend too much time on their smartphone
too-much-smartphone.passage: Just over half of U.S. adults say they spend too much time on their smartphone

tried-to-cut-back.name: Tried to cut back on smartphone use
tried-to-cut-back.passage: 45% of U.S. adults say they've tried to cut back on their smartphone use over the past 12 months.

smartphone-hurts-sleep.name: Smartphone hurts the amount of sleep they get
smartphone-hurts-sleep.passage: Much larger shares say their smartphones hurt than help the amount of sleep they get (41% vs. 5%).

census-commute-2019.name: U.S. Census Bureau: one-way travel time to work (ACS 2019)

average-commute.name: Average one-way commute
average-commute.passage: the average one-way commute in the United States increased to a new high of 27.6 minutes in 2019

hour-plus-commute.name: Commutes of 60 minutes or longer
hour-plus-commute.passage: the percentage of workers reporting commutes of 60 minutes or longer increased from 7.9% in 2006 to 9.8% in 2019

bls-ebs-2026.name: BLS Employee Benefits in the United States (March 2026): paid leave

paid-vacation.name: Access to paid vacation
paid-vacation.passage: Paid vacation leave was available to 80 percent of private industry workers

paid-sick-leave.name: Access to paid sick leave
paid-sick-leave.passage: 81 percent had access to paid sick leave

sick-leave-hospitality.name: Paid sick leave in leisure and hospitality
sick-leave-hospitality.passage: Access to paid sick leave for private industry workers ranged from 58 percent for the leisure and hospitality industry

pew-pto-2023.name: Pew Research Center: more than 4 in 10 U.S. workers don't take all their paid time off (2023)

take-less-pto.name: Take less paid time off than offered
take-less-pto.passage: Some 46% of U.S. workers who receive paid time off from their employer

worry-falling-behind.name: Would worry about falling behind at work
worry-falling-behind.passage: A similar share (49%) say they'd worry about falling behind at work if they took more time off.

coworkers-guilt.name: Would feel bad about coworkers taking on their work
coworkers-guilt.passage: Some 43% of workers who don't take all their time off say they'd feel badly about their co-workers

lsc-justice-gap-2022.name: Legal Services Corporation: The Justice Gap (2022), civil legal problems of low-income households

any-problem.name: Low-income households with at least one civil legal problem
any-problem.passage: 3 in 4 (74%) low-income households experienced 1+ civil legal problems in the past year.

no-enough-help.name: Civil legal problems without enough legal help
no-enough-help.passage: Low-income Americans do not get any or enough legal help for 92% of their substantial civil legal problems.

cost-barrier.name: Did not seek help because of cost
cost-barrier.passage: 1 in 2 (46%) of those who did not seek legal help for one or more problems cite concerns about cost as a reason why.

consumer.name: Consumer issues
consumer.passage: One-half (50%) of low-income households experienced a problem related to consumer issues.

health-care.name: Health care
health-care.passage: Nearly two in five (39%) low-income households experienced a problem related to health care in the past year.

income-maintenance.name: Income maintenance
income-maintenance.passage: More than one-third (34%) of all low-income households experienced a problem related to income maintenance

housing.name: Housing
housing.passage: One-third (33%) of all low-income households experienced a civil legal problem related to housing in the past year.

family-safety.name: Family and safety
family-safety.passage: About one-quarter (26%) of all low-income households have experienced at least one problem related to family matters

education.name: Education
education.passage: Nearly one in five (19%) low-income households has experienced a civil legal problem related to education in the past year.

211-impact-2025.name: United Way 211 Impact Snapshot 2025: top referral categories

legal-consumer-safety.name: Legal, consumer and public safety assistance (#4)
legal-consumer-safety.passage: Referrals for legal, consumer, and public safety assistance

oecd-wellbeing.name: OECD Well-being Framework: Work-life balance indicators

long-hours.name: Employees working very long hours
long-hours.passage: The portion of the labor force that works very long hours (more than 50 hours a week).

leisure-personal-care.name: Time devoted to leisure and personal care
leisure-personal-care.passage: spending time with friends, going to the movies, pursuing hobbies, sleeping, eating, etc.

gender-gap-hours.name: Gender gap in hours worked, paid and unpaid

Q14.name: Q14: To what extent do you have the opportunity for leisure activities?

sdg-targets.name: UN SDG targets bearing on time, chores and paperwork

5.4.name: Target 5.4: recognize and value unpaid care and domestic work
5.4.passage: Recognize and value unpaid care and domestic work through the provision of public services,

5.4-data.name: Women's share of unpaid domestic and care work (SDG report 2024)
5.4-data.passage: On average, each day, women spend 2.5 times more hours on unpaid domestic and care work than men.

11.2.name: Target 11.2: safe, affordable, accessible transport for all
11.2.passage: By 2030, provide access to safe, affordable, accessible and sustainable transport systems for all,

16.3.name: Target 16.3: equal access to justice for all
16.3.passage: Promote the rule of law at the national and international levels and ensure equal access to justice for all

16.6.name: Target 16.6: effective, accountable and transparent institutions
16.6.passage: Develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels

16.9.name: Target 16.9: legal identity for all
16.9.passage: By 2030, provide legal identity for all, including birth registration

idleness.name: Idleness (leisure)
idleness.passage: daydream, brood, dream, recall old times, give way to fantasies, remember, relax, have fun, play

career.name: Career wellbeing
career.passage: The first element is about how you occupy your time or simply liking what you do every day: your Career Well-Being.
